chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal and Muhassin bin Ahmad, from Yunus bin Yaqoub, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at a man from the people of Medina who had bought something for his dependents and was carrying it. When the man saw him, he felt shy/embarrassed. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You bought it for your dependents and carried it to them. By Allah, had it not been for the people of Medina, I would have loved to buy something for my dependents and then carry it to them myself.'

key_terms.أَمَا وَ اللَّهِ: An emphatic oath meaning 'By Allah, indeed'.
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ: The people of Medina, referring to the general populace or specific social class whose customs were respected.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam al-Sadiq carrying goods for his family in Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s humility and awareness of social etiquette (*adab*), distinguishing between the intrinsic virtue of manual labor and the contextual respect for Medina’s elite status. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing personal piety with social consciousness, showing that the Imam’s restraint was not a denial of the act's merit but a consideration of communal norms. This narrative reinforces the principle that religious practice is often nuanced by local customs and the dignity of the community.
